documents.unit: Center for the Advancement of Teaching
documents.title: Setting Expectations and AI Policy
tiers: Use freely permitted with no acknowledgement
documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance telling instructors to write a syllabus AI policy covering permitted use, citation, ethics, consequences and open communication, with sample language. It also explains how SCAI treats AI misuse as cheating or plagiarism and cautions that Turnitin AI checkers are unreliable.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule itself: it offers four approaches ("Use Prohibited", "Use only with prior permission", "Use only with acknowledgment", freely permitted) that "can be taken as is or combined", and SCAI judges cases "based on the reporting professor's AI syllabus policy", so the decision is delegated to instructors.

units.why: The guidance tells faculty to specify which AI tools are permitted and how they may be used: "Begin by specifying which AI tools". It is a communication directive, so P09 (state AI expectations in the syllabus or assignment) fits better than P04, which is about who decides.
units.anchor: Begin by specifying which AI tools
units.frag_start: Begin by specifying which AI tools
units.policy: Instructors begin by specifying which AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Grammarly, AI-driven research assistants) are permitted for assignments, projects, or examinations, and clearly state how they should or should not be used.

units.why: The example says instructors "may explicitly allow AI for preliminary research, brainstorming, or improving clarity in writing". Brainstorming is the most specific permitted-use type (P15); the writing-clarity part (P18) is secondary and one type is chosen. Consensus coding after reconciliation: policy_type=P04.
units.anchor: explicitly allow AI for preliminary research, brainstorming, or improving clarity in writing
units.policy: Instructors may explicitly allow AI for preliminary research, brainstorming, or improving clarity in writing, while restricting its use for original critical analysis or assessments designed to measure personal mastery.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: policy_type=P15. Coder B: policy_type=P04. The sentence tells instructors what they 'may explicitly allow AI for' (preliminary research, brainstorming, clarity). It is instructor discretion over what to permit, which P04 (let each instructor set the rule) covers; P15 describes a use students may make, and the next unit already carries that. Final: policy_type=P04.

units.why: The same sample allows ChatGPT-type tools "for initial idea generation and clarifying concepts", a permitted use as a helper for understanding concepts (P12). Consensus coding after reconciliation: policy_type=P15.
units.anchor: may be used for initial idea generation and clarifying concepts
units.resolution_why: Coder A: policy_type=P12. Coder B: policy_type=P15. The passage permits AI 'for initial idea generation and clarifying concepts'. Idea generation is the first-named use and is brainstorming (P15); clarifying concepts is a second use in the same clause. P15 is chosen as the lead use; P12 (tutor) is not chosen because the clause leads with idea generation. Final: policy_type=P15.

units.why: Sample language says AI-generated content as your own work "is strictly prohibited unless explicitly permitted by the instructor". The key move is the prohibited-unless-permitted default, so P06 rather than P19. Consensus coding after reconciliation: policy_type=P19.
units.anchor: is strictly prohibited unless explicitly permitted by the instructor
units.policy: Direct use of AI-generated content as the student's own analytical or creative work is strictly prohibited unless explicitly permitted by the instructor.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: policy_type=P06, unit_stance=restrict. Coder B: policy_type=P19, unit_stance=prohibit. The sample language reads 'direct use of AI-generated content as your own analytical or creative work is strictly prohibited unless explicitly permitted by the instructor.' A split this one sentence into a prohibition (P06) and B into a prohibition (P19) plus an exception (P04, may). The rule is a single prohibition with an instructor-permission exception, so it is one unit: must-not, P19 (do not have AI produce submitted work), restrict. P06 is for the case where a syllabus is silent, which this is not. B's separate unit for the exception clause is merged here. Final: policy_type=P19, unit_stance=restrict.

units.why: The guidance says AI use "must be transparently acknowledged", which is a disclosure requirement (P24); no tool or prompt detail is demanded, so not P25.
units.anchor: the use of AI tools must be transparently acknowledged
units.policy: Instructors explain to students that the use of AI tools must be transparently acknowledged, and establish guidelines for citing AI-generated ideas or content.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor=instructor. Coder B: actor=student. The sentence is 'Clearly explain to students that the use of AI tools must be transparently acknowledged', an instruction to the instructor to communicate the rule. The addressee of the sentence is the instructor, so actor is instructor (A); the student-facing version is the next sample-language unit. Final: actor=instructor.

units.why: "Offer students explicit examples of correct citation formats for AI-generated content" advises instructors on how students cite AI; closest to P25 (how to cite), though no tool or prompt details are mandated.
units.anchor: Offer students explicit examples of correct citation formats for AI-generated content.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: policy_type=P25. Coder B: policy_type=P24. 'Offer students explicit examples of correct citation formats for AI-generated content' is about how to cite AI output, which P25 (cite the tool, prompt, output) covers; P24 is the duty to disclose, which the preceding unit states. Final: policy_type=P25.

units.why: Sample language: "Any ideas, concepts, or text developed with the assistance of an AI tool must be clearly cited". A student-facing disclosure and citation rule: P24.
units.anchor: must be clearly cited in your submissions
units.policy: Any ideas, concepts, or text developed with the assistance of an AI tool must be clearly cited in student submissions.

units.why: Sample language states "Failure to attribute AI-generated content appropriately will be considered plagiarism": nondisclosure itself is the violation (P28), more specific than P36. Consensus coding after reconciliation: modality=informs.
units.anchor: Failure to attribute AI-generated content appropriately will be considered plagiarism
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality=must, unit_stance=restrict. Coder B: modality=must-not, unit_stance=prohibit. 'Failure to attribute AI-generated content appropriately will be considered plagiarism' states a consequence, not a new duty (the duty to cite is the previous unit). A coded must, B must-not; neither fits a consequence statement, so informs. AI is allowed with attribution, so unit_stance is restrict, not prohibit. Final: modality=informs, unit_stance=restrict.

units.why: The guidance asks faculty to "Highlight ethical responsibilities related to AI use, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and avoidance of bias or misrepresentation", naming ethical concerns: P53.
units.anchor: emphasizing transparency, fairness, and avoidance of bias or misrepresentation
units.policy: Instructors highlight ethical responsibilities related to AI use, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and avoidance of bias or misrepresentation.

units.why: Sample language: students "are expected to critically reflect on the ethical implications of using AI", with discussion of "bias, representation, privacy, and fairness". Names ethical concerns (P53); it is course discussion, not a reflection log (P26).
units.anchor: students are expected to critically reflect on the ethical implications of using AI

units.why: "Clearly outline the consequences for violating the course's AI policy" asks that penalties be stated up front: P37.
units.anchor: Clearly outline the consequences for violating the course’s AI policy
units.policy: Instructors clearly outline the consequences for violating the course's AI policy, aligning them with the institution's broader academic integrity policies.

units.why: The same sample names "unauthorized use on assessments" as misuse, so unauthorized AI on assessments is barred. P22 chosen because it addresses assessments specifically.
units.anchor: unauthorized use on assessments
units.policy: Unauthorized use of AI tools on assessments is misuse of AI tools.
units.resolution_why: Coder A only. The sample sentence names 'unauthorized use on assessments' as misuse of AI tools. This is a real (if brief) statement that unauthorized AI on assessments is misuse; kept. Stance is restrict because the wording is conditional on authorization.

units.why: Sample language classes "unauthorized use on assessments, failure to cite appropriately, or submission of fully AI-generated work" as "violations of academic integrity policies": P36. Consensus coding after reconciliation: modality=informs.
units.anchor: will be treated as violations of academic integrity policies, potentially leading to disciplinary action
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality=must, unit_stance=restrict. Coder B: modality=informs, unit_stance=prohibit. The sample language says misuse 'will be treated as violations of academic integrity policies, potentially leading to disciplinary action'. This is a statement of consequence (informs), not a new duty. Stance is restrict because only the listed misuse is treated as a violation. Final: modality=informs, unit_stance=restrict.

units.why: Sample language: "If you are unsure whether the use of an AI tool aligns with course guidelines, please reach out to me directly". Ask-first rule: P10.
units.anchor: If you are unsure whether the use of an AI tool aligns with course guidelines

units.why: "Be clear with your students about how AI will be used in your classroom" and point to the syllabus policy: communicating expectations at course start (P09).
units.anchor: Be clear with your students about how AI will be used in your classroom.
units.frag_end: that may come up during the discussion.

units.why: Faculty are advised to consider gray areas such as "Grammarly or other such tools" and give examples of acceptable practice. Grammarly is a prose tool, so P18 over P07. Consensus coding after reconciliation: modality=should.
units.anchor: consider how you will handle instances of students using
units.policy: Instructors may provide specific examples of what may or may not be considered acceptable practices, and consider how they will handle students using Grammarly or other tools that may seem like gray areas.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality=may. Coder B: modality=should. 'Consider how you will handle instances of students using Grammarly or other such tools' is advice to the instructor, so should (B) rather than may (A). Final: modality=should.

units.why: "Explain to your students that you may be using an AI checker like Turnitin" tells instructors to disclose detector use. This is P40 (checkers used to identify misuse), not P47, which concerns instructor AI use in teaching.
units.anchor: you may be using an AI checker like Turnitin
units.policy: Instructors explain to students that they may be using an AI checker like Turnitin to determine if their work is original.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality=should. Coder B: modality=may. The text says to 'Explain to your students that you may be using an AI checker like Turnitin'. The instruction to explain is the policy (should); 'may be using' describes the instructor's possible action. Final: modality=should.

units.why: Students should grasp "the importance of using AI as a tool rather than as a substitute for their own thinking": students stay the primary thinker (P32). Consensus coding after reconciliation: actor=instructor.
units.anchor: using AI as a tool rather than as a substitute for their own thinking
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor=student. Coder B: actor=instructor. The sentence is addressed to the instructor ('express to them the importance of using AI as a tool rather than as a substitute for their own thinking'). Actor is instructor (B); A coded student because the content concerns student behavior. Final: actor=instructor.

units.why: "be ready to have this conversation not only on the first day of class but also as a reminder throughout the rest of the term" asks for repeated communication of expectations: P09.
units.anchor: but also as a reminder throughout the rest of the term
units.policy: Instructors be ready to have the AI conversation on the first day of class and as a reminder throughout the term.
units.resolution_why: Coder A only. The page tells instructors to be 'ready to have this conversation not only on the first day of class but also as a reminder throughout the rest of the term'. This is a distinct rule about repeating the AI conversation; B's first-day unit does not cover it. Kept.

units.why: The note says "AI checkers like Turnitin are not 100% reliable", a statement that detectors are unreliable: P39.
units.anchor: AI checkers like Turnitin are not 100% reliable.

units.why: Instructors with high scores or suspicion are invited to 'come and see the CAT staff' to rethink the assessment structure; redesign of assessment around AI, P35.
units.anchor: assist you in rethinking the assessment structure
units.policy: Instructors with repeatedly high plagiarism scores or strong suspicion of cheating may see CAT staff, who can assist in rethinking the assessment structure so learning outcomes are met but cheating is less likely.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality=should. Coder B: modality=may. The note offers help: 'please come and see the CAT staff and we can assist you in rethinking the assessment structure'. It invites instructors to use CAT support; it is not a duty or advice to redesign. May (B) fits, should (A) is stronger than the text. Final: modality=may.

units.why: SCAI "is charged with handling all university cases of academic misconduct", including cheating or plagiarism with AI or automated tools. AI misuse is handled as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: cheating or plagiarism based on how a student may have used AI
units.policy: FIU's Student Conduct and Academic Integrity (SCAI) office handles all university cases of academic misconduct, including cheating or plagiarism based on how a student may have used AI (or automated tools).

units.why: The cheating definition includes unauthorized use of 'automated tools', defining AI misuse as misconduct (P36). Consensus coding after reconciliation: modality=informs, unit_stance=restrict.
units.anchor: the unauthorized access or use of any materials, information, study aids, automated tools
units.frag_end: on any academic assignment or exercise.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality=informs, unit_stance=restrict. Coder B: modality=must-not, unit_stance=prohibit. The text defines cheating ('the unauthorized access or use of any materials, information, study aids, automated tools'). A coded informs; B coded must-not. It is a definition of misconduct, so informs. Stance is restrict because only unauthorized use is cheating. Final: modality=informs, unit_stance=restrict.

units.why: The plagiarism definition covers work 'authored by another person or automated tool without proper acknowledgment'; misconduct definition, P36 (it also implies disclosure but is framed as misconduct). Consensus coding after reconciliation: modality=informs, unit_stance=restrict.
units.anchor: the submission of any work authored by another person or automated tool
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality=informs, unit_stance=restrict. Coder B: modality=must-not, unit_stance=prohibit. The text defines plagiarism as submitting work authored by 'another person or automated tool without proper acknowledgment'. A coded informs; B coded must-not. A definition, so informs; restrict because acknowledged use is not plagiarism. Final: modality=informs, unit_stance=restrict.

units.why: 'The burden of proof is on the university' sets how AI misconduct cases are decided, a fairness safeguard for accused students; nearest P64.
units.anchor: The burden of proof is on the university for all academic misconduct cases.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor=all, policy_type=UNCOVERED. Coder B: actor=admin, policy_type=P64. 'The burden of proof is on the university for all academic misconduct cases' is a fairness safeguard for accused students, which P64 covers. A coded UNCOVERED with actor all; the burden rests on the university, so actor is admin. B's P64 is closer to the definition than UNCOVERED. Final: actor=admin, policy_type=P64.

units.why: Faculty 'are required to report all misconduct instances to SCAI', an integrity-process rule, P36.
units.anchor: FIU faculty are required to
units.frag_end: report all misconduct instances to SCAI
units.policy: FIU faculty are required to report all misconduct instances to SCAI.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: policy_type=UNCOVERED. Coder B: policy_type=P36. 'FIU faculty are required to report all misconduct instances to SCAI' sends AI cases into the integrity process, which P36 covers. A coded UNCOVERED; the type's 'handled by integrity processes' fits, so UNCOVERED is not needed. Final: policy_type=P36.

units.why: SCAI decides AI cases "based on the reporting professor's AI syllabus policy", so the instructor's own syllabus rule is the standard. This delegates the rule to instructors: P04.
units.anchor: they make this determination based on the reporting professor’s AI syllabus policy

units.why: "Each of these approaches and examples can be taken as is or combined" leaves the choice to instructors: P04.
units.anchor: can be taken as is or combined into something more comprehensive
units.frag_start: Each of these approaches and examples
units.resolution_why: Coder A only. 'Each of these approaches and examples can be taken as is or combined into something more comprehensive' tells instructors they may mix the approaches; this is a real statement about how to build a policy. Kept.

units.why: The page lists approaches to a syllabus AI policy: "Use Prohibited", freely permitted, "Use only with prior permission", "Use only with acknowledgment". These are named categories of use: P05.
units.anchor: Use Prohibited
units.policy: The CAT offers four approaches to an AI syllabus policy: use prohibited; use freely permitted with no acknowledgement; use only with prior permission; use only with acknowledgment.

documents.title: Sample Language - Use of AI
documents.summary: A short Academic Affairs syllabi-program handout reproducing five alternative sample syllabus statements about AI, from encouraging to prohibiting. Instructors pick or adapt one.
documents.stance_why: The document is a menu of sample statements ranging from "We encourage the use of AI tools" to "AI-generated submissions are not permitted", so it takes no single stance and leaves the choice to instructors.

units.why: The sample says "We encourage the use of AI tools to inform yourself about the field", an encouraging default (P02).
units.anchor: We encourage the use of AI tools to inform yourself about the field

units.why: "(1) An AI cannot pass this course" says the student, not the AI, does the work: P32.
units.anchor: An AI cannot pass this course

units.why: "AI contributions must be attributed and true" combines attribution and verification. Attribution is the main policy (P24); the truth element would be P31.
units.anchor: AI contributions must be attributed and true

units.why: "The use of AI tools should be open and documented" asks for documented use. P26 chosen over P24 because it speaks of documentation. Consensus coding after reconciliation: policy_type=P24.
units.anchor: The use of AI tools should be open and documented
units.resolution_why: Coder A: policy_type=P26. Coder B: policy_type=P24. 'The use of AI tools should be open and documented' asks for disclosure, not for logs or transcripts, so P24 (B) rather than P26 (A). Final: policy_type=P24.

units.why: 'This policy covers any generative AI tool' including text, artwork, video and audio defines scope (P61).
units.anchor: This policy covers any generative AI tool, such as ChatGPT, Elicit, etc.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor=all. Coder B: actor=student. The sample syllabus statement ('This policy covers any generative AI tool') is addressed to students in the syllabus text. Actor student (B); A coded all. Final: actor=student.

units.why: "You are discouraged from using AI tools UNLESS under direct instruction" discourages AI without forbidding it: P03.
units.anchor: You are discouraged from using AI tools UNLESS under direct instruction from your instructor
units.frag_end: from your instructor to do so.

units.why: "Please contact your instructor if you are unsure or have questions BEFORE using AI" is ask-first: P10.
units.anchor: Please contact your instructor if you are unsure or have questions BEFORE using AI

units.why: "You must indicate what part of the assignment was written by AI and what was written by you" requires disclosure of which parts: P24 (not P27, which is code-specific).
units.anchor: you must indicate what part of the assignment was written by AI
units.frag_start: If AI is permitted to be used

units.why: "No more than 25% of an assignment should be created with AI" is a percentage cap on AI-produced work: P16.
units.anchor: No more than 25% of an assignment should be created with AI

units.why: "You must sign the AI contract that you understand and agree to these policies" requires a signed agreement. No type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: You must sign the AI contract that you understand and agree to these policies.
units.uncovered_note: Students must sign an AI contract acknowledging they understand and agree to the AI policy.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: policy_type=UNCOVERED. Coder B: policy_type=P09. The sample says 'You must sign the AI contract that you understand and agree to these policies.' B coded P09, which is about the instructor stating AI expectations in the syllabus. Here the student signs an acknowledgment, which no type covers, so UNCOVERED (A) with a note. Final: policy_type=UNCOVERED.

units.why: "All work submitted in this course must be your own" is ownership of submitted work: P29.
units.anchor: All work submitted in this course must be your own.

units.why: "Contributions from anyone or anything else- including AI sources, must be properly quoted and cited" treats AI as an outside source needing citation: P24.
units.anchor: including AI sources, must be properly quoted and cited every time they are used
units.resolution_why: Coder A: unit_stance=permit. Coder B: unit_stance=require. The sample is headed 'Allowing if cited' and says AI sources 'must be properly quoted and cited every time they are used'. A coded permit, B require. The sample permits AI conditional on citation, so unit_stance is permit (A). Final: unit_stance=permit.

units.why: "Failure to do so constitutes an academic integrity violation" makes non-citation the violation: P28. Consensus coding after reconciliation: modality=informs.
units.anchor: Failure to do so constitutes an academic integrity violation
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality=must, unit_stance=restrict. Coder B: modality=informs, unit_stance=prohibit. 'Failure to do so constitutes an academic integrity violation' states a consequence of not citing. A coded must/restrict, B informs/prohibit. A consequence statement is informs; AI is allowed when cited, so restrict. Final: modality=informs, unit_stance=restrict.

units.why: "I will follow the institution's policy to the letter in those instances" says misuse goes through the institutional process: P36.
units.anchor: I will follow the institution’s policy to the letter in those instances.
units.resolution_why: Coder A only. The instructor says 'I will follow the institution's policy to the letter in those instances' when a student does not cite. This is a commitment about enforcement (P36) that the sample states in its own sentence. Kept.

units.why: The reason given: 'writing, analytical, and critical thinking skills are part of the learning outcomes', so skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: writing, analytical, and critical thinking skills are part of the learning outcomes
units.resolution_why: Coder B only. The clause 'writing, analytical, and critical thinking skills are part of the learning outcomes of this course' is the stated reason for the ban in the same sentence as A's rule unit, and is a rationale (P41). Kept.

units.why: The prohibit sample says "all writing assignments should be prepared by the student", with writing skills as outcomes. Who prepares the work: P19.
units.anchor: all writing assignments should be prepared by the student
units.frag_start: Since writing, analytical, and critical thinking
units.resolution_why: Coder A only (B coded the first half of the same sentence as a separate rationale unit). 'All writing assignments should be prepared by the student' is the rule; the rationale clause about learning outcomes is a separate unit. Kept both.

units.why: "Developing strong competencies in this area will prepare you for a competitive workplace" is a reason for doing the work yourself. P41 (skill-building) is nearest; P44 is about teaching AI use. Consensus coding after reconciliation: phase=general.
units.anchor: Developing strong competencies in this area will prepare you for a competitive workplace.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: phase=course-start, policy_type=P41. Coder B: phase=general, policy_type=P44. 'Developing strong competencies in this area will prepare you for a competitive workplace' is the stated reason for the AI ban in the 'Prohibit AI' sample. A coded P41 (AI shortcuts practice that builds skill), B P44 (teach AI use as a professional skill). The sentence refers to writing and critical thinking skills, not AI skills, and justifies the ban, so P41. It is a rationale (informs, general). Final: phase=general, policy_type=P41.

units.why: "AI-generated submissions are not permitted and will be treated as plagiarism" bans AI-generated submissions: P19.
units.anchor: AI-generated submissions are not permitted and will be treated as plagiarism

units.why: "Unauthorized and/or unacknowledged collaboration on any work ... is plagiarism" is the existing collaboration rule the AI sentence extends, so AI is treated like an outside collaborator (P45). Consensus coding after reconciliation: modality=informs, unit_stance=neutral.
units.anchor: Unauthorized and/or unacknowledged collaboration on any work
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality=must-not, unit_stance=restrict. Coder B: modality=informs, unit_stance=neutral. 'Unauthorized and/or unacknowledged collaboration on any work ... is plagiarism' is a definition (informs). A coded must-not/restrict. It does not name AI itself, but it sets up the AI sentence that follows and both coders chose P45; kept as P45 neutral. Final: modality=informs, unit_stance=neutral.

units.why: "Content generated by an Artificial Intelligence third-party service ... without proper attribution or authorization is another form of plagiarism": P36. Consensus coding after reconciliation: modality=informs.
units.anchor: Content generated by an Artificial Intelligence third-party service or site
units.resolution_why: Coder A: phase=general, unit_stance=restrict. Coder B: phase=when-misuse, unit_stance=prohibit. The sample says AI-generated content 'without proper attribution or authorization is another form of plagiarism'. Both coders coded must-not, A in general phase and B in when-misuse. It is a definition of plagiarism, so informs and general; restrict because attributed or authorized use is not plagiarism. Final: phase=general, unit_stance=restrict.

units.why: "If you are unsure ... please reach out to me to discuss it as soon as possible" is ask-the-instructor: P10.
units.anchor: please reach out to me to discuss it as soon as possible
units.frag_start: If you are unsure about whether

documents.title: Guidelines for the Effective and Responsible Use of AI in Dissertations
documents.summary: University Graduate School guidelines for AI in theses, dissertations and research proposals. They list acceptable and unacceptable uses, require full disclosure to the committee in the preliminary pages, assign duties to students, mentors, programs and UGS, and warn on risks, privacy and detectors.
documents.stance_why: The document allows listed uses ("Acceptable Uses" such as grammar, outlining, explaining concepts) provided they are disclosed, while banning generating substantive portions, so AI is permitted with conditions; programs may add stricter standards but the UGS text itself sets this rule.

units.why: The purpose section says guidelines "outline the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) assisted tools in theses and dissertations": an institution-level framework, P56.
units.anchor: outline the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) assisted tools in theses
units.resolution_why: Coder A only. 'These guidelines outline the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) assisted tools in theses and dissertations' states the purpose of the guidelines (P56 framework preamble). B coded only the scope sentence. Kept.

units.why: Scope is "all aspects of graduate research for thesis bound master's and doctoral students": who is covered, P61.
units.anchor: apply to all aspects of graduate research for
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor=student, policy_type=P61. Coder B: actor=admin, policy_type=P62. A coded actor student and P61, B coded admin and P62. The sentence sets scope ('apply to all aspects of graduate research for thesis bound master's and doctoral students'), which P61 covers; P62 is for rules, and the scope is the students it binds, so student. Final: actor=student, policy_type=P61.

units.why: Programs "may establish additional discipline-specific standards" and students "are responsible for understanding and adhering to both": layered research rule, P62. Consensus coding after reconciliation: actor=admin, phase=general, modality=may, policy_type=P04.
units.anchor: individual programs, schools, and departments may establish additional discipline-specific standards
units.policy: Individual programs, schools, and departments may establish additional discipline-specific standards; students are responsible for understanding and adhering to both sets of requirements.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor=student, phase=before-course, modality=must, policy_type=P62. Coder B: actor=all, phase=general, modality=informs, policy_type=P04. 'Individual programs, schools, and departments may establish additional discipline-specific standards' gives programs authority. A coded student/before-course/must/P62, B all/general/informs/P04. The subject is the program, the verb is 'may', so actor admin, modality may, general phase; P04 covers deferring the rule to the unit. Final: actor=admin, phase=general, modality=may, policy_type=P04.

units.why: 'Students are responsible for understanding and adhering to both sets of requirements', an ownership duty, P29. Consensus coding after reconciliation: policy_type=P62.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding and adhering to both sets
units.policy: Students are responsible for understanding and adhering to both the University Graduate School expectations and the additional standards of their program, school, or department.
units.resolution_why: Coder B only. 'Students are responsible for understanding and adhering to both sets of requirements' is a real duty. B coded P29 (students own what they submit); the duty is to follow two layers of research rules, so P62. Kept.

units.why: "these guidelines may be updated to reflect emerging best practices" shows a provisional policy: P54.
units.anchor: these guidelines may be updated to reflect emerging best practices
units.frag_start: As AI technologies evolve, these guidelines

units.why: Graduate education aims "to cultivate the critical-thinking skills required to conduct independent research", a learning rationale: P41.
units.anchor: cultivate the critical-thinking skills required to conduct independent research

units.why: "AI tools may support research and writing, but they do not replace scholarly judgment": AI must not replace thinking, P32.
units.anchor: they do not replace scholarly judgment, expertise, or ethical decision-making

units.why: "Responsible AI use upholds the core values of Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)" states principles: institution-level framework, P56.
units.anchor: Responsible AI use upholds the core values of Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)

units.why: Theses "must meet all RCR standards, including those governing attribution, authorship, research integrity, and originality": research rule, P62.
units.anchor: must meet all RCR standards, including those governing attribution, authorship, research integrity, and originality

units.why: Students must "Use AI tools responsibly and in accordance with the principles of responsible conduct of research": general principle, P56.
units.anchor: Use AI tools responsibly and in accordance with the principles of responsible conduct of research.

units.why: Students must "Understand that AI tools often produce confabulations (or hallucinations)": output can be wrong, P31.
units.anchor: AI tools often produce confabulations (or hallucinations) which are false, nonsensical, or incorrect information
